**Normal:** incremental most of the time, with an occasional stale-cursor full scan. 'No cursor' sustained means incremental mode is broken, not idle — that once disabled incremental scans for good while every scan still reported success.

**Next:** 'Scan Mode Decisions' and 'Incremental Bailouts' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: NATS Backlog
panels.description:
**Work waiting in the scanner's queue** (stream JE_BOX): scan requests, users and folders not picked up yet. This is 'how far behind is it?', and it is readable even while the connector is asleep.

**Normal:** 0 between scans. Growing with no pods running means the connector is not waking up.

**Next:** 'NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog' below for the shape over time.

panels.title: In Flight
panels.description:
**Work handed to a pod and not finished yet.**

**Normal:** a few while a scan runs, 0 otherwise. Stuck high while Items Sent stays at 0 is the signature of a hung connector.

**Next:** 'Pods Up' and 'Restarts (1h)'.

panels.title: Redelivered
panels.description:
**Work being retried after a failure.** A message is retried up to 5 times (JOBENGINE_MAX_DELIVER) before it is moved to the dead-letter queue.

**Normal:** 0. A connector that fails and retries in a loop shows up here and nowhere else.

**Next:** 'Deferrals' (a saturated user also spends retries) and the Dead Letter Queue row.

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running now**, as the autoscaler reports them.

**Normal:** 0 between scans, 1–3 during one.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Replicas' below for the history.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description:
**The most scanner pods the autoscaler may start** (chart setting autoscaling.maxReplicas, 3 by default, and it can differ per environment).

**Normal:** read it against Replicas and the backlog: at the ceiling with a growing backlog means the scanner cannot go faster. Being at the ceiling with a draining backlog is routine with a low ceiling, not trouble.

**Next:** 'NATS Backlog'.

panels.title: Backlog Slope
panels.description:
**How fast the scanner's backlog is growing**, in messages per second. This is exactly what one of the autoscaler's rules looks at.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0.5 the autoscaler adds pods.

**Next:** 'KEDA — trend-based vs threshold' below.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The scanner's queue over time.** Pending = waiting, ack pending = being worked on, redelivered = being retried. Each message is a scan request, a user or a folder, so a small number can hide a lot of work.

**Normal:** spikes at the start of a scan that drain to 0. Ack pending held up while Items Sent stays at 0 means the connector is stuck.

**Next:** 'Scanner Throughput' to compare with the work actually done.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running, pods wanted, and the ceiling.**

**Normal:** pods stay up ~15 minutes after the work ends (cooldown 900s, scale-down window 600s). 'It scaled ten minutes ago and is still the same' is configuration, not a bug.

**Next:** the three KEDA signal panels below show why it scaled.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Scanner pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — the scanner scales to zero when there is no work, so 0 is the normal resting state, not an outage. 'Should be running and is not' is 0 pods WITH a backlog, which the queue panels in this row show.

**Next:** 'NATS Backlog'.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Scanner container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Restarts usually mean the pod ran out of memory (limit 256 MiB) or failed its health check.

**Next:** the Runtime board, memory panels.

panels.title: Found
panels.description:
**Files the scanner saw, counted over the selected time range.** Same number as in Totals, repeated so this row reads on its own.

**Normal:** see Totals. Unlike a rate, this does not drop to 0 after a short scan ends.

**Next:** 'Scanner Throughput' for when it happened.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description:
**Files the scanner found but could not hand on for indexing**: bad file data plus failures to send, added together. This is the headline loss count.

**Normal:** 0. Which of the two it was matters: bad data is a problem with what Box returned; a failed send is the sender or the message queue.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' for the split.

panels.title: Sent

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="sent"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))

panels.description:
**Files handed on for indexing, counted over the selected time range.** Same number as in Totals.

**Normal:** close to Files Discovered (window). Unlike a rate, this does not drop to 0 after a short scan ends.

**Next:** 'Scanner Throughput' for when it happened.

panels.title: Folder Duration — mean / p95

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**How long one folder takes: listing it in Box plus queuing and sending what it contains.** This is the connector's real unit of work. The mean is the typical folder — multiply it by a folder count to estimate a bigger tenant. The p95 is how slow the slowest 5% were, and it does not multiply.

**Normal:** around half a second to one second, most of it Box's own response time (measured: mean 0.62 s over 33,000 folders). A p95 far above the mean means a few very large or slow folders.

**Next:** 'Folder Duration — p50 / p95 / p99' below, and 'API Call Duration p95 by Endpoint' to see whether Box is the slow part.

panels.title: Slots Held
panels.description:
**Per-user work slots this connector holds right now, across all scanner pods.** Box limits traffic per user, so the connector lets at most BOX_USER_MAX_CONCURRENCY (5 by default) folders of the same user run at once, shared by every pod.

**Normal:** 0 when idle. Slots near the cap with deferrals rising means that cap is what limits speed.

**Next:** 'User Slots — held vs requeued' below and 'Deferrals' in the Box API row.

panels.title: Scanner Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**How fast files are seen, sent and failed**, as a rate. Three near-parallel lines; the question is the gap between them.

**Normal:** sent tracks discovered and failed stays at 0. A scan shorter than ~30 seconds may not show here at all — the stats above still count it.

**Next:** the Pipeline board graphs the gap explicitly ('Item Loss').

panels.title: Folder Duration — p50 / p95 / p99

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**Folder time as percentiles, computed over the whole selected time range.** One folder = one listing plus what it queues and sends.

**Normal:** p50 and p95 under about a second. The latest value is the one to read; it uses everything in the range, so it works for short scans too.

**Next:** 'Folder Duration — mean / p95' for the mean, which is the number to multiply.

panels.title: Scan Durations — three different units

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**Three different timings, drawn together for scale only — they are not comparable.** Fan-out = logging in, listing all users and queuing one scan per user; it does NOT include scanning their folders. Incremental = one whole incremental scan, including its enrichment. Root folder = one user's top-level folder only, not their whole tree.

**Normal:** fan-out in seconds, root folder under a few seconds, incremental from seconds to minutes. 'How long did the whole scan take' cannot be answered by the connector: a full scan is many messages on many pods with no single owner.

**Next:** the Pipeline board's Cost & Prediction row.

panels.title: Scanner Items by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every file the scanner handled**, as counts for the whole range — same colours as the line chart beside it.

**Normal:** almost everything green (sent). Yellow is expected absence (the file was already in the trash or gone); red needs a look.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when; the Pipeline board splits it by datasource.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Scanner Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When files ended in each outcome**, as a rate. 'Skipped inactive' means the file was already in Box's trash when its folder was listed — the scanner's part of Files Gone.

**Normal:** mostly sent. Do not add 'skipped inactive' to the event stream's deletions: they are different moments for possibly the same file.

**Next:** the Data Quality — Files Gone row.

panels.title: Folders by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every folder the scanner visited**, as counts for the whole range.

**Normal:** mostly forked (its subfolders were queued) and sent. A publish failure loses the whole subtree below that folder.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folders_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folders_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folders_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Folders by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When subfolders were queued, skipped or failed to queue**, as a rate. Every subfolder becomes its own message; 'skipped collab' is a folder owned by another user, left for that user's own scan.

**Normal:** forked and skipped collab only. 'Publish failed' is the worst silent failure: until that message is retried, the folder's whole subtree is not scanned.

**Next:** 'Folders Forked' and 'Folders Skipped' for the counts.

panels.title: User Slots — held vs requeued
panels.description:
**Where the scanner holds itself back.** Box limits traffic per user, so each user gets a fixed number of slots shared by all pods. A folder that finds no free slot waits (BOX_USER_SLOT_WAIT_SEC, 10 s), then is re-queued as a fresh message — 'requeues', the normal sign of contention. After BOX_USER_SLOT_MAX_REQUEUE (50) re-queues it is instead put back for retry — a 'deferral' — which spends one of its 5 attempts.

**Normal:** requeues climbing with deferrals at 0 is healthy. Deferrals above 0 is the last step before a folder and everything below it is thrown away.

**Next:** 'Deferrals' and the Dead Letter Queue row.

panels.title: KEDA — ack-capacity vs threshold
panels.description:
**One autoscaler rule: work in progress on the scanner queue, against its threshold** (red line, 1000). Pods wanted = in-progress messages divided by the threshold, rounded up.

**Normal:** far below the line.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Replicas' above.

panels.title: KEDA — trend-based vs threshold
panels.description:
**Another autoscaler rule: is the queue growing?** Above 0.5 messages per second it adds pods; it becomes active at 0.1.

**Normal:** 0 most of the time, short positive bumps at the start of a scan.

**Next:** 'Backlog Slope'.

panels.title: KEDA — pending-wakeup vs threshold
panels.description:
**The rule that wakes the scanner from zero:** a single waiting message is enough. The red line is the scale threshold (1000). A fourth rule, 'pipeline full', is not configured in this chart (its capacity is empty), so it is deliberately not drawn.

**Normal:** spikes when a scan is requested that drain to 0. Pending above 0 with no pods running for more than a minute or two means the wake-up is not working.

**Next:** 'Pods Up'.

panels.title: Box API — Rate Limits & Quota
panels.description: In an API connector the scarce resource is Box's rate limit: roughly 16.67 req/s for the whole app, shared across every pod. None of these series carries a tenant label — the HTTP client has no datasource_id in scope — so this row cannot be filtered by datasource. Attribution lives in the scanner funnel instead.

panels.title: API Calls (window)
panels.description:
**Requests sent to the Box API, counted over the selected time range — attempts, not logical calls.** A failed request is retried up to BOX_MAX_RETRIES (3), so one file lookup can be four requests. Includes both scanner and content pods.

**Normal:** roughly one request per folder page plus one per enriched file. Requests growing faster than files means the connector is retrying. Box allows about 16.7 requests per second for the whole app, shared across all pods.

**Next:** 'API Calls by Endpoint (window)' for where they went.

panels.title: Limiter Wait p95
panels.description:
**How long requests waited on the connector's own speed limit before going out** (95th percentile, last 5 minutes). This is the early warning: the connector is holding itself back before Box has to.

**Normal:** near 0. Rising means pods are hitting BOX_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC (8 per pod); lowering that setting must move this first — if it does not, the signal is broken.

**Next:** 'Back-pressure — ours vs Box's'.

panels.title: 429s (window)

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_api_rate_limit_hits_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_api_rate_limit_hits_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_api_rate_limit_hits_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)

panels.description:
**Times Box refused a request for going too fast (HTTP 429), over the selected time range.** This is the late signal: Box has already said no. Each one is retried after the wait Box asks for.

**Normal:** 0. Known blind spot: 429s on the file download path used by content pods are not counted here, so this is scanner and enrichment traffic only.

**Next:** 'API Calls by Status' and 'Limiter Wait p95'.

panels.title: Deferrals
panels.description:
**Scan messages put back for retry because their user had no free slot, over the selected time range.** For a folder this only happens after it has already been re-queued BOX_USER_SLOT_MAX_REQUEUE (50) times; a user's first top-level scan has no re-queue path and is put back straight after waiting. Each one spends one of the message's 5 attempts (JOBENGINE_MAX_DELIVER), and past that the folder and everything below it is thrown away.

**Normal:** 0. Anything above zero means the per-user limits are too tight for this tenant.

**Next:** 'Redelivered' and the Dead Letter Queue row.

panels.title: Requeues
panels.description:
**Folders re-queued as a fresh message because their user had no free slot, over the selected time range.** This is back-pressure working: a fresh message starts with a full set of attempts, so waiting never pushes a folder toward being thrown away.

**Normal:** above 0 under load is normal. Worry only if 'Deferrals' beside it also rises.

**Next:** 'User Slots — held vs requeued' in the Scanner row.

panels.title: API Calls by Status (window)
panels.description:
**Box API responses by HTTP status**, as counts for the whole range — same colours as the line chart beside it.

**Normal:** nearly all 200. 404 is expected (an item removed between listing and reading); 429 means Box is rate-limiting us; 4xx/5xx need a look.

**Next:** 'Back-pressure — ours vs Box's' below for rate limiting.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: API Calls by Status (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Box API responses by status code**, as a rate. 'transport_error' is a request that never got an answer (connection reset, timeout, DNS), kept apart so 'Box refused us' and 'we never reached Box' are not the same thing.

**Normal:** almost all 200. 429 = too fast; 401/403 = credentials or permissions; 5xx or transport errors = Box or the network.

**Next:** '429s (window)' and 'API Call Duration p95 by Endpoint'.

panels.title: API Calls by Endpoint (window)

targets.expr: (sort_desc(sum by (endpoint, status) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_api_calls_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))) > 0

panels.description:
**What the selected time range cost in Box API requests, per endpoint and status.** Box limits requests per app, so this budget is what binds, and 'how many did this scan spend' is the number to plan with.

**Normal:** folder listings on top during a full scan. A large count on the per-user event pull means the last-access lookup is the expensive part.

**Next:** 'API Calls by Endpoint (rate, 5m)' for when.

panels.title: API Calls by Endpoint (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Which Box API endpoint the traffic goes to**, as a rate. The four event-stream endpoints are kept apart on purpose: reading the change cursor is one or two pages, the admin-log backfill up to 200 pages per refresh, and the per-user pull runs once for every user.

**Normal:** folder listings dominate during a scan; file and collaboration lookups during enrichment. A short scan may not show here — the table below counts it.

**Next:** 'API Calls by Endpoint (window)' for totals.

panels.title: Back-pressure — ours vs Box's
panels.description:
**The four signs of saturation, in the order they appear.** First folders cannot get a user slot and are re-queued; then the connector's own speed limit makes requests wait; deferrals appear only once folders run out of re-queues; Box's 429 refusals come last.

**Normal:** all near 0. Requeues alone under load are fine. 429s mean Box is already refusing; deferrals mean folders are close to being lost.

**Next:** 'Deferrals' and '429s (window)'.

panels.title: API Call Duration p95 by Endpoint
panels.description:
**How long Box takes to answer, per endpoint** (95th percentile). Only the round trip: the time waiting on our own speed limit is excluded, so 'is Box slow?' and 'are we holding ourselves back?' stay separate.

**Normal:** folder listings around half a second. For file content this is only the time until the download starts, NOT the download itself — reading it as the download time is wrong by orders of magnitude.

**Next:** 'Transfer p95 by size_bucket' in the Content row for the download.

panels.title: Rate Limiter Wait — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**How long requests waited on the connector's own speed limit**, as percentiles. Measured from 1 millisecond up.

**Normal:** near 0. Sustained waits of a second or more mean BOX_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC (8 per pod) is what limits the scan.

**Next:** 'Back-pressure — ours vs Box's'.

panels.title: Augmenter — box-connector-be-go
panels.description: The augment path re-fetches each previously discovered file from Box to attach collaborations and an approximated last-access date. It is the only source of ACLs in the connector today.

panels.title: Augmenter Items by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every item the augmenter enriched**, as counts for the whole range.

**Normal:** almost everything sent. 'sent without ACL' is a degraded success: the item went out without its permissions.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**What happened to each file the enrichment step re-fetched from Box to add who can access it (collaborations) and when it was last accessed.** Exactly one outcome per file. 'Sent without ACL' = the access list could not be read, so the file was sent without it: degraded success, not plain success. 'Missing' = Box answered 404, the file is gone.

**Normal:** mostly sent. A growing 'sent without ACL' share means access data is incomplete. A file counted as missing here is also counted by a separate 'not found' series — never add the two.

**Next:** the Pipeline board's Augmenter row, per datasource.

panels.title: last_access Coverage
panels.description:
**How much of the last-access date we send is real rather than unknown** (hit rate), with the number of access events loaded per second underneath it.

**Normal:** a steady hit rate. A falling hit rate while events stop loading means the event store is stale, not that the data is bad.

**Next:** 'last_access Result' and 'Events Loaded into the Store' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Batch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**How long one enrichment batch takes**, as percentiles over the selected time range.

**Normal:** seconds to a few minutes depending on batch size. This is the one enrichment panel that cannot be split by datasource (the timing is taken before the datasource is known); it still filters by pod.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Items by Outcome' for how much each batch did.

panels.title: Content — box-connector-be-go-content
panels.description: CONNECTOR_MODE=content streams Box file bytes into content-service. These series are labeled by datasource_access_id, not datasource_id: the URN content is handed carries only access, file_id and user_id, so the datasource_id genuinely does not exist in this mode.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Content pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — content also scales to zero, so 0 is not an outage. 'Should be running and is not' is 0 pods with a fetch backlog.

**Next:** 'Fetch Backlog'.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Content container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Restarts usually mean the pod ran out of memory (limit 256 MiB) or failed its health check.

**Next:** the Runtime board with Component = Content.

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**File downloads requested, counted over the selected time range**, any outcome. Every delivery counts, so a request retried after a failure counts again.

**Normal:** whatever was asked for.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)'.

panels.title: Fetch Time

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**How long one file fetch takes, end to end.** The mean is total fetch time over fetch count — multiply it by a number of fetches to estimate a bigger job. The p95 is the slowest 5%.

**Normal:** seconds for ordinary office files. Fetch cost grows with file size, so read the mean against 'Transfer Rate': if the mean rises while the transfer rate holds, the files got bigger and nothing is wrong; if the transfer rate falls, something really got slower.

**Next:** the Pipeline board's Content row for success vs failure and per size.

panels.title: Transfer Rate

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 0.001)

panels.description:
**Transfer speed while actually transferring**: bytes delivered divided by the time spent fetching, not by elapsed time.

**Normal:** steady across runs. Read it against 'Fetch Time': if fetch time rises while this stays flat, the files got bigger; if this falls, something really got slower. Unlike 'Upload Rate' it does not drop to 0 when idle.

**Next:** 'Transfer p95 by size_bucket'.

panels.title: Errors

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", success="false"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", success="false"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", success="false"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)

panels.description:
**File fetches that did not succeed**, for any reason, over the selected time range.

**Normal:** 0, but not every error is a problem — a file deleted since the scan is expected.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' for the colours.

panels.title: Upload Rate
panels.description:
**Bytes per second sent to the content service**, averaged over the last 5 minutes of wall-clock time. Counted as what the content service confirmed receiving, not what Box declared.

**Normal:** 0 whenever nothing is running; a short burst may read near 0.

**Next:** 'Transfer Rate' for the speed of the transfers themselves.

panels.title: Fetch Backlog
panels.description:
**File-fetch requests waiting**, bulk and interactive ('See content') queues together.

**Normal:** 0 between jobs. Growing with no content pods means they are not waking up.

**Next:** 'NATS — Content Consumer Backlog' for the two queues apart.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When fetches happened and how they ended**, as a rate. 'NONE' is shown as success.

**Normal:** bursts when a job runs. Read the time axis, not the height: a burst of a few fetches in seconds spread over 5 minutes is a tiny number. For how many, use the bars beside it.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)'.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (window)

targets.expr: (sum by (error_code) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) > 0

panels.description:
**Where every fetch ended up, counted over the selected time range.** The total is in 'Fetches'; this is how it split. Green = fine. Yellow = expected (the file is gone or over the size limit). Orange = back-pressure (rate limited, timeout). Red = needs action (credentials, permissions, internal or queue failures).

**Normal:** mostly green.

**Next:** the Pipeline board's 'Fetch Errors by error_code' table.

panels.title: Transfer p95 by size_bucket

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, size_bucket) (rate(box_content_transfer_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**How long the download from Box plus upload to the content service takes, per file size** (95th percentile, successful fetches). Answers 'is the slowness per file or per byte?'. 'Unknown' means Box did not say the file size, not a zero-byte file.

**Normal:** small files well under a second, large ones longer in proportion to size.

**Next:** the Pipeline board has the failure version of this panel.

panels.title: Uploaded Bytes (rate)
panels.description:
**Bytes sent to the content service per second over time**, as confirmed by the content service.

**Normal:** bursts when a job runs, 0 otherwise.

**Next:** 'Transfer Rate' for the speed while transferring.

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**Both content queues over time**: the bulk queue (classifier) and the interactive queue ('See content', a person waiting in the UI), shown separately so an interactive backlog is not averaged away. Pending = waiting, ack pending = in progress, redelivered = being retried (at most 3 attempts).

**Normal:** spikes that drain to 0. Anything on the interactive queue that does not drain within seconds means someone is staring at a spinner.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Replicas'.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Content pods running, pods wanted, and the ceiling** (3 by default).

**Normal:** 0 when idle; pods stay up ~15 minutes after the work ends (cooldown 900s, scale-down window 600s).

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Trigger Signals'.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Trigger Signals
panels.description:
**Three of the content autoscaler's rules, all on the bulk queue**: work in progress, queue growth, and waiting messages, with their thresholds in the legend. The 'pipeline full' rule is not configured in this chart.

**Normal:** far below the thresholds. Any waiting message wakes the pods from zero.

**Next:** 'KEDA — interactive-wakeup' beside it.

panels.title: KEDA — interactive-wakeup signal vs threshold
panels.description:
**The rule that wakes the content pods for the interactive queue.** The scanner has no equivalent: it exists so a single 'See content' request wakes the pods even when the bulk queue is empty. Without it, scale-to-zero would turn every such request into a timeout.

**Normal:** 0, or brief spikes that drain within seconds.

**Next:** 'Pods Up' in this row.

panels.title: Data Quality — Files Gone
panels.description: Box answers 'how many files are no longer there?' at THREE stages, and they are deliberately not summable: each is a different moment in the pipeline and is diagnosed differently. The incremental one is the cleanest signal in the whole set — it comes from an explicit ITEM_TRASH/DELETE event from Box, not from a NOT_FOUND inferred after the fact.

panels.title: Gone — seen in trash by the scan

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="skipped_inactive"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="skipped_inactive"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="skipped_inactive"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Files that were already in Box's trash when the scanner listed their folder**, over the selected time range.

**Normal:** a small number on an active tenant. Do not add it to the other 'Gone' stats: each is a different moment, possibly for the same file.

**Next:** 'Files Gone by stage'.

panels.title: Gone — deleted per the event stream

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_changes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="deleted"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_changes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="deleted"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_changes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="deleted"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Files reported deleted or trashed by Box's event stream during incremental scans**, over the selected time range. The cleanest 'gone' signal: Box said so explicitly.

**Normal:** follows how much users delete. 0 when no incremental scan ran.

**Next:** 'Incremental Changes by Outcome' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Gone — 404 on augment re-fetch

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Files found by an earlier scan that Box no longer had (404) when the enrichment step went back for them**, over the selected time range.

**Normal:** small. Expected churn, not a failure.

**Next:** 'Files Gone % (augment)' to put it in proportion.

panels.title: Gone — 404 on content fetch

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Files that were gone (404) when the content pods went to download them**, over the selected time range — the latest of all the 'gone' moments.

**Normal:** small. Do NOT add it to the other stages: content only fetches a requested subset, so it has a different denominator. It is here because a 404 on download is evidence a file is gone, which otherwise shows only as a content error.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)'.

panels.title: Files Gone by stage (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When files turned out to be gone, by the stage that noticed**: already in trash at scan time, deleted per the event stream, 404 on enrichment, 404 on download. Four series, never one number.

**Normal:** small bumps that follow user deletions. The enrichment line is the same event as a separate 'not found' counter; that one is not drawn so nothing is counted twice.

**Next:** the stats above for the counts.

panels.title: Augment Items

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Files the enrichment step processed, over the selected time range** — the denominator for the percentage beside it.

**Normal:** the number of files sent for enrichment. A ratio needs this: 100% of 4 files and 100% of 40,000 are the same number and completely different news.

**Next:** 'Files Gone % (augment)'.

panels.title: Files Gone % (augment)

targets.expr: 100 * ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)), 1))

panels.description:
**Share of the files the enrichment step touched that Box no longer had.**

**Normal:** a low percentage. Always read it with 'Augment Items' beside it, because the percentage alone hides how small the sample is.

**Next:** 'Gone — 404 on augment re-fetch'.

panels.title: Data Loss — Dead Letter Queue
panels.description: What was lost. The scanner funnel can close perfectly and work can still have been discarded here: a message that exhausts its deliveries ends up in the DLQ leaving no trace in items_processed. See PLAN-deferral-dlq.md.

panels.title: DLQ Depth
panels.description:
**Scan messages given up on after 5 attempts and parked in the dead-letter queue (DLQ_CONSUME_BOX).** For the scanner each one is a folder plus its entire subtree, so this count does not measure the damage: one message cost 7 files when it hit a small folder, and would cost thousands near the top of a tree.

**Normal:** 0. Any other value means a scan quietly returned less than the tenant holds — and the connector's own funnel cannot show it, because Items Sent still equals Files Discovered for what was seen. Each message names the folder: nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_BOX <seq>.

**Next:** 'DLQ Depth over time' for when, and 'Deferrals' for the usual cause.

panels.title: Lost to DLQ (window)
panels.description:
**Messages that failed every retry and were given up on in the selected range.** Each one is a folder — and everything below it — that was not indexed while its scan still reported success.

**Normal:** 0. To see which ones: each message carries the folder and the last error — `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_BOX <seq>`. Counted from the stream's sequence number, so a purge or the DLQ's own size limit does not hide anything.

**Next:** 'DLQ Depth over time' beside it, for when it started.

panels.title: DLQ Depth over time
panels.description:
**When work started landing in the dead-letter queue.**

**Normal:** flat at 0. A step up marks the moment a scan started losing folders; it is the only outside evidence, because the connector reports no failure.

**Next:** 'Deferrals' and 'Redelivered' around the same time.

options.content:
### Box Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/box/box-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [Box Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-box-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *where, for which datasource, and at what cost*. Use the datasource selector at the top to narrow everything to one datasource.

**Totals count only what happened inside the time range** — narrow it to one scan to describe one Box tenant.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Scanner — Discovery & Funnel
panels.description: The funnel checks itself: files_discovered minus the sum over every items_processed outcome is zero unless some exit path in processFolder is uninstrumented. Everything in this row is per datasource, which is what turns 'something is losing files' into 'this tenant is losing files'.

panels.title: Scanner Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**What happened to every file the scanner saw**, as a rate, stacked by outcome. The 'discovered' line is not part of the stack — it is the total the stack should add up to.

**Normal:** the stack reaches the discovered line, almost all of it sent. A scan shorter than ~30 seconds may not show here; the Overview's Totals row counts it. Filter by $box_datasource_id to see one datasource.

**Next:** 'Item Loss (discovered − sent)' below.

panels.title: Folders by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When subfolders were queued, skipped or failed to queue**, per datasource. Every subfolder becomes its own message; 'skipped collab' is a folder owned by another user, left for that user's own scan.

**Normal:** forked and skipped collab only. 'Publish failed' means a whole subtree was not scanned until that message is retried.

**Next:** 'Folders Forked' on the Overview.

panels.title: Discovery → Sent Conversion
panels.description:
**Share of discovered files that were sent** (sent ÷ discovered).

**Normal:** 1 (100%). Files already in Box's trash also lower it, so a little under 1 is expected. Only meaningful while a scan runs; short scans may not show.

**Next:** 'Item Loss' beside it for the absolute number.

panels.title: Item Loss (discovered − sent)
panels.description:
**Files seen minus files sent, per second.** Includes files skipped because they were in Box's trash.

**Normal:** near 0. This is a different question from the conversion ratio: 99% on a huge tenant can leak more files than 60% on a tiny one.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' to see which outcome the gap is.

panels.title: Users Skipped by Reason (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Users skipped, by reason, as a rate.** These users' files were never discovered, so the file funnel above cannot show this loss at all.

**Normal:** only deactivated and terms-of-service. Permission denied is broken configuration; traverse failed is a real error and is counted on every retry.

**Next:** 'Users Skipped by Reason' on the Overview for counts.

panels.title: Scanner — Cost & Prediction
panels.description: What a unit of work costs, and what a bigger tenant would cost. The three durations at the right are three different units of work and are NOT comparable with each other — they share a panel for scale only.

panels.title: Folder Duration — p50 / p95 / p99

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**Folder time as percentiles over the selected time range, per datasource.** One folder = one Box listing plus what it queues and sends: the connector's real unit of work.

**Normal:** p50 and p95 under about a second. Read the latest value; it covers the whole range.

**Next:** 'Mean Cost per Folder' beside it.

panels.title: Mean Cost per Folder
panels.description:
**Average seconds per folder.** Multiply it by a folder count to estimate a larger tenant: 'if this enterprise grew 10x, how much folder work is that?'.

**Normal:** around half a second to a second, most of it Box's own response time. Only drawn while folders are being processed.

**Next:** 'API Call Duration p95 by Endpoint' on the Overview to see if Box is the slow part.

panels.title: Scan Durations — three different units

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_fanout_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_root_folder_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**Three different timings, drawn together for scale only.** Fan-out = logging in, listing users and queuing one scan per user; it does NOT include scanning their folders, which happens in other messages on other pods. Incremental = a whole incremental scan including its enrichment. Root folder = one user's top-level folder only.

**Normal:** fan-out in seconds, root folder under a few seconds. If fan-out and folder times come out similar, something is not measuring what it should.

**Next:** 'Incremental Duration' in the next row.

panels.title: Scanner — Incremental
panels.description: An incremental run reads Box's /events stream from the stored cursor, dedupes, applies deletes and augments the changed files inline. It lists no folders at all, so the scanner's folder panels stay flat while an incremental runs.

panels.title: Incremental Changes by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**What incremental scans did with each changed file**, as a rate: upserted (sent again), deleted, delete failed, or skipped. 'Deleted' is Box's cleanest 'file gone' signal — an explicit delete or trash event.

**Normal:** mostly upserted, some deleted, delete failed at 0. A failed delete leaves a removed file in the index.

**Next:** 'Incremental Bailouts'.

panels.title: Incremental Duration — p50 / p95 / p99

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_scanner_incremental_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_id=~"$box_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.description:
**How long one incremental scan takes**, as percentiles over the selected time range. Unlike the fan-out, this really is the whole job: reading changes, removing duplicates, deletes and enrichment.

**Normal:** seconds to a few minutes, growing with how much changed.

**Next:** 'Scan Mode Decisions' to check incremental scans are running at all.

panels.title: Incremental Bailouts (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Incremental scans that switched themselves to a full scan** because too much had changed — more than BOX_INCREMENTAL_MAX_RATIO (5% by default) of the known files.

**Normal:** 0 or rare. Frequent bailouts are expensive: each one is a full scan.

**Next:** 'Scan Mode Decisions' beside it.

panels.title: Scan Mode Decisions (increase, 5m)
panels.description:
**Which mode each scan was allowed to run in, and why**, counted per 5 minutes. No cursor = nothing to read changes from. Cursor stale = the last full scan is older than BOX_INCREMENTAL_MAX_AGE_HOURS (168 h). Cursor fresh = incremental.

**Normal:** mostly incremental. No cursor sustained means incremental is broken, not idle — that once disabled it for good while every scan reported success. Cursor stale sustained means the scan schedule and that setting disagree. This is the decision before the run: an incremental run can still bail out to full, so incremental minus bailouts is what really stayed incremental.

**Next:** 'Incremental Bailouts'.

panels.title: Scanner — Saturation
panels.description: The two things that bound scan speed: per-user admission slots (Box rate-limits per impersonated user and the cap is shared across pods) and the client-side rate limiter against the app-wide ceiling.

panels.title: Folder Work In-Flight & User Slots Held
panels.description:
**Folders being worked on right now, and per-user slots held**, summed over scanner pods. Not split by datasource: the slots are per user, and the deferral counter is per datasource, so the two cannot be joined.

**Normal:** flat at 0 while pods sleep. Slots at the cap (BOX_USER_MAX_CONCURRENCY, 5 per user) with deferrals rising means that cap limits speed. Flat at 0 WITH load would mean the counting is broken.

**Next:** 'Slot Contention by Datasource' beside it.

panels.title: Slot Contention by Datasource (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**What happens when a user has no free slot, per datasource.** Requeue = the folder is re-queued as a fresh message with a full set of attempts. Deferral = it is put back for retry, spending one of its 5 attempts; for folders that only happens after BOX_USER_SLOT_MAX_REQUEUE (50) re-queues.

**Normal:** requeues up with deferrals at 0 is healthy contention. Deferrals above 0 is the last warning before folders and their subtrees are thrown away. Both at 0 = no contention.

**Next:** 'DLQ Depth' on the Overview.

panels.title: Augmenter — Outcomes & Coverage
panels.description: The augment path is the only source of ACLs in the connector: the scanner's collaboration fetch is commented out in folder_work.go to save API tokens.

panels.title: Augmenter Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**What happened to each file the enrichment step re-fetched**, as a rate per datasource. Exactly one outcome per file, so the stack adds up to the batch. 'Sent without ACL' = the access list could not be read and the file went out without it: degraded success, and also the only count of access-list failures. 'Missing' = Box answered 404.

**Normal:** mostly sent. Rising 'sent without ACL' means incomplete access data; 'get file failed', build or send failures should be 0.

**Next:** 'Skipped Not-Found' below.

panels.title: last_access Result (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Last-access lookups that found a real date (hit) or not (miss)**, as a rate. As a ratio it tells how much of the last-access date we send is real rather than unknown.

**Normal:** a steady hit share.

**Next:** 'Events Loaded into the Store' beside it.

panels.title: Events Loaded into the Store (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Box access events loaded into the connector's last-access store on each refresh**, per second. This is what the hit rate depends on.

**Normal:** bumps at each refresh. A hit rate falling while this goes to 0 is a stale store, not a data problem.

**Next:** 'last_access Result'.

panels.title: Skipped Not-Found (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Files Box no longer had (404) when the enrichment step went back for them**, per datasource. The same event as 'missing' in the outcome panel; it exists separately so alerts can ignore this expected signal.

**Normal:** small. Never add it to the outcome panel — that would count the same files twice.

**Next:** 'Files Gone' row on the Overview.

panels.title: Content — Fetch & Streaming
panels.description: Filtered by $box_access_id, not $box_datasource_id: content mode is handed a URN carrying only access, file_id and user_id, so the datasource_id genuinely does not exist here. The 'unknown' value is the bounded sentinel for failures that happen before the URN is parsed.

panels.title: Content Fetches by error_code (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**How file fetches ended**, as a rate, filtered by $box_access_id. NONE = success. Timeouts and too-large are outcome codes, not separate counters. The NAK_* codes are failures in the message-queue handling itself (unreadable request, or the reply could not be sent); those messages are retried.

**Normal:** mostly NONE. A short job may barely show — the Overview's bar chart counts it.

**Next:** 'Fetch Errors by error_code' table below.

panels.title: Transfer p95 by size_bucket — success

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, size_bucket) (rate(box_content_transfer_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**How long successful download-plus-upload takes, per file size** (95th percentile). Sizes are cut at 1 MiB, 10 MiB and 100 MiB; 'unknown' means Box did not send the size.

**Normal:** grows with size. If small files are slow too, the cost is per file (Box latency), not per byte.

**Next:** 'Transfer p95 by size_bucket — failure' beside it.

panels.title: Transfer p95 by size_bucket — failure

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, size_bucket) (rate(box_content_transfer_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="false"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**The same timing for transfers that failed, per file size.** The size is known before the transfer starts, so failures can be split too: a 80 MiB file dying halfway and a 2 KiB file that never opens are different incidents.

**Normal:** empty. Long times on large files point at timeouts; short times on small files at access errors.

**Next:** 'Fetch Errors by error_code'.

panels.title: Content Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**How long one successful fetch takes end to end**, as percentiles. Failures are kept out so a slow failure does not distort the success numbers.

**Normal:** seconds for ordinary files; the p99 reflects the largest files.

**Next:** 'Content Fetch p95 by access_id' to find which datasource is slow.

panels.title: Content Fetch Bytes — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Size of successfully fetched files**, as percentiles. Not split by datasource. The size steps go from 1 KiB to 256 MiB; anything larger falls off the top and the percentile cannot place it.

**Normal:** depends on the tenant; mostly under a few MiB.

**Next:** 'Transfer p95 by size_bucket — success'.

panels.title: Uploaded Bytes (rate)
panels.description:
**Bytes sent to the content service per second, per datasource access**, as confirmed by the content service.

**Normal:** bursts during jobs, 0 otherwise.

**Next:** 'Average Bytes per Fetch'.

panels.title: Content Fetch p95 by access_id

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, datasource_access_id) (rate(box_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod", datasource_access_id=~"$box_access_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**Which datasource access is slow** (95th percentile of successful fetches). 'unknown' means the request failed before the connector could tell which datasource it belonged to.

**Normal:** similar lines. One line far above the rest points at that tenant's files or Box account.

**Next:** 'Transfer p95 by size_bucket — success' to see whether it is just bigger files.

panels.title: Fetch Errors by error_code (increase, 1h)
panels.description:
**Fetch errors by code over the last hour**, for triage. NAK_* codes are failures in the message-queue handling, not Box refusing us.

**Normal:** empty. NOT_FOUND is expected (file deleted since the scan); credential or permission codes need configuration fixes; timeouts and rate limiting are back-pressure.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by error_code' for when.

panels.title: Content Requests In-Flight
panels.description:
**File fetches running right now**, summed over content pods. This is the content side's measure of how busy it is.

**Normal:** 0 when idle; at most 10 per pod (contentFetch.workers) during a job.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Replicas' on the Overview.

panels.title: Average Bytes per Fetch
panels.description:
**Average bytes per successful fetch.** An average only: one 1 GB file and a thousand 1 KB files land on the same point as a thousand medium files.

**Normal:** stable for a given tenant. Use it as a quick sanity check; the size percentile panels are the real answer.

**Next:** 'Content Fetch Bytes — p50 / p95 / p99'.

panels.title: Connection Tests by Outcome
panels.description:
**Connection tests answered in the selected range**, by outcome: success, partial (passed, but some objects could not be read), credential_error, permission_denied, timeout, error, publish_failed (the verdict could not be delivered).

Totals add up every test in the range, and a test redelivered after a pod shutdown is counted on the pod that answers it.

**Normal:** mostly success. partial or permission_denied means the Box app can see less than the customer expects; credential_error, timeout, error or publish_failed point at the connector or at Box.

**Next:** 'Connection Test Outcomes (rate, 5m)' beside it for when they happened, and 'Connection Test Errors by Code (rate, 5m)' for the reason.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Connection Test Outcomes (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When connection tests were answered**, by outcome, stacked. A test shorter than a scrape interval can read 0 here and still be counted in 'Connection Tests by Outcome'.

**Normal:** short green bursts when someone tests a connection. Sustained red or orange means tests keep failing.

**Next:** 'Connection Test Errors by Code (rate, 5m)' for the reason.

panels.title: Connection Test Duration by Depth (p95)
panels.description:
**How long a connection test takes end to end**, 95th percentile by requested depth. A connect test takes under a second, a size test seconds to a couple of minutes, and a debug walk up to its 55-minute cap.

**Normal:** each depth stays near its usual time. A debug walk sitting at the cap means it was cut short, and a connect test taking many seconds means Box or the credential fetch is slow.

**Next:** 'Connection Test Outcomes (rate, 5m)' for tests that ended in timeout.

panels.title: Connection Test Errors by Code (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Failed connection tests by the standard error code** carried in the reply, stacked. Counted once the reply has been delivered or given up on, so a redelivered test is not counted twice.

**Normal:** nothing. A steady code points at a cause: a credential code means the customer's Box app or its secret, a permission code means the app was not granted access.

**Next:** 'Connection Tests by Outcome' for the matching totals; the connector logs name the failing call.

panels.title: Connection Test Objects Skipped (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Objects a connection test could not read** and reported on their own node while it carried on, by level (user or folder). A test with any is answered as partial.

**Normal:** 0. A steady rate means the Box app cannot read some users or folders, so a scan would miss them too.

**Next:** 'Connection Tests by Outcome' for how many tests were partial; the test result in the UI names the objects.

panels.title: Registration State by Pod
panels.description:
**Whether each pod has registered itself with the registration service**, shown as the current state over time: registered, pending (no answer yet), unreachable (the registry or network is failing), rejected (the registry refused, retrying), rejected_final (refused for good), build_failed (the registration could not be built), lane_missing (no test-connection lane is being served), disabled (registration is switched off).

The registration series exist only on builds that include the registration-metrics change, so older pods show No data here. Connector pods scale to zero, so a pod's line exists only while a scanner pod is running.

**Normal:** registered, after a short pending at start-up. lane_missing, rejected_final and build_failed are the states to alert on: no other panel reports them, and the pod is not registering. unreachable held for longer than a deploy takes is worth alerting on too.

**Next:** 'Registration Attempts by Result' for whether attempts are still failing, and the connector logs for the reason.

targets.expr: (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="disabled"}) * 1) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="pending"}) * 2) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="unreachable"}) * 3) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="rejected"}) * 4) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="registered"}) * 5) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="rejected_final"}) * 6) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="build_failed"}) * 7) + on(pod) (max by (pod) (box_registration_state{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod",state="lane_missing"}) * 8)

panels.title: Registration Attempts by Result
panels.description:
**Registration attempts made in the selected range**, by result: success (the registry accepted it), rejected (the registry refused it), failed (no answer: the registry was unreachable or failing). Totals add up every attempt of every pod in the range.

**Normal:** a success at start-up and one about every 6 hours when the pod renews. Rejected or failed attempts that keep coming mean the pod is not (re-)registering. A pod can still read registered while renewals fail, so this is the panel that shows it.

**Next:** 'Registration Attempts (rate, 5m)' beside it for when, and 'Registration State by Pod' for the pod's current state.

targets.expr: sum by (result) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(box_registration_attempts_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(box_registration_attempts_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(box_registration_attempts_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$box_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Registration Attempts (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When registration attempts happened**, by result, stacked. An attempt is rare, so a single one can read near 0 here and still be counted in 'Registration Attempts by Result'.

**Normal:** a short green mark at start-up and every 6 hours. A steady orange or red line means the pod keeps trying and the registry keeps refusing it or not answering.

**Next:** 'Registration State by Pod'; the registration service board for its side.

panels.title: Since Last Success
panels.description:
**How long since any pod last registered successfully**, measured from the newest success among the selected pods.

**Normal:** under 6 hours, because the connector re-registers every 6 hours. Well beyond that means renewals are failing even if the state still reads registered. No data means no scanner pod is running (they scale to zero) or the pod's build predates the registration metrics.

**Next:** 'Registration Attempts by Result' for what the attempts are returning.
